item.title: I Put a Spell On You Featuring Faith Evangeline – Tue, Oct 27 (SOLD OUT)
item.description:
Showtimes: 07:30 PM (SOLD OUT)

"There's an old deserted mansion on an old forgotten road

Where the better ghosts and goblins always hang out

One night they threw a party in a manner a la mode

And they cordially invited all the gang out”…

Sincerely, Faith

item.title: Jazz, TX Presents: Jazzmeia Horn – Wed, Oct 28 (SOLD OUT)
item.description:
Showtimes: 07:30 PM (SOLD OUT)

Jazzmeia Horn brings a powerful, expressive voice to the world of modern jazz. Drawing on her gospel roots, she explores themes of love and social change through her music. She has won both the 2013 Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition and the 2015 Thelonious Monk International Jazz Competition.

Born in Dallas and raised in a church-going family, Ms. Horn studied at Booker T. Washington High School for the Performing and Visual Arts and The New School in New York City. Her debut album, "A Social Call," earned a Grammy nomination, and "Love and Liberation" earned another. Today she tours the world and teaches through The Jazz Horn International Vocal Initiative.

As always, our kitchen and bar will be open for dinner service.

See you at the show!

item.title: "The Best is Yet to Come" - A Tribute to Frank Sinatra with Wyatt Michael and the Jazz, TX House Band – Thu, Oct 29
item.description:
Showtimes: 07:00 PM, 09:30 PM

Jazz, TX brings back our favorite vocal phenom Wyatt Michael, best know for his performance of "Mack the Knife" on season 21 of The Voice.

Backed by the Jazz, TX House Band, Wyatt pays tribute to all the classic Sinatra hits like "You Make Me Feel So Young," "Fly Me To The Moon," "Pennies From Heaven," and many others.

More about Wyatt Michael:

From a young age, Wyatt Michael studied the piano and while he never connected with the instrument as a child, his appreciation for music was instilled. Wyatt began writing music with his brother and over the next few years, they began performing their original music in the rock band Chasing Avenir. As Chasing Avenir released their first EP “Blue” and played at the National Theater in Richmond, VA, Wyatt was introduced to the jazz standards and immediately fell in love with them.

Once the decision was made to become a jazz singer, Wyatt joined forces with Chris Whiteman and began work on his first solo album “Renaissance.” Released on November 8th 2019, “Renaissance” is made up of songs written by David Mann, composer of the classic “In the Wee Small Hours of the Morning,” that have never before been released to the public. Wyatt was given special permission from Mann’s son and estate to bring these songs to life.

After only two years of full-time singing, Wyatt was featured on season 21 of “The Voice” where he turned the chairs of both Kelly Clarkson, and Ariana Grande during the Blind Auditions stage. Wherever Wyatt Michael performs, he brings the passion, emotion, and musicianship of the golden age of music—honoring the legacy of the giants who came before him and carrying it forward for generations to come.

As always, our kitchen and bar will be open for dinner service.

See you at the show!

item.title: Villains & Magic: A Disney Halloween at Jazz, TX! – Fri, Oct 30 (SOLD OUT)
item.description:

**A wickedly fun Disney Halloween celebration! Costumes highly encouraged!**

See you at the show!

item.title: Midnight Set with the Demetreis Thornton Quartet | “Swing Low” Jazz Bass Trombone – Fri, Oct 30
item.description:
Showtimes: 11:59 PM

Been to one of our regular shows? You know the drill: great sets, dinner service, a polished room. Midnight, that goes out the window.

The Midnight Set is jazz unplugged: looser, louder, no rules. Late-night bites, strong drinks, good company, and the kind of playing that only comes out after hours.

This set it's bass trombonist Demetreis Thornton, out of El Paso and one of the sharpest young voices coming up today. His sound pulls from Curtis Fuller, Steve Davis, Benny Golson, Slide Hampton, and Art Blakey, and he's already shared stages with heavyweights like Gary Smulyan, Andre Hayward, Brad Leali, and Mike Sailors. Since landing in Austin in 2023, he's been everywhere, composing, arranging, teaching, and playing across Central Texas.

Tonight he brings "Swing Low," his showcase for an instrument most bands treat as "trombone 4." Demetreis treats it as a lead voice: songbook standards, hard bop, and ballads, all filtered through a sound that's entirely his own. See you at midnight.

The kitchen will be offering our late night menu and the bar will be fully be open for drink service!
